spots.n: Golden Gate Bridge → Sausalito bike & ferry loop
spots.s: THE San Francisco date: pedal 8 easy miles over the bridge, linger over waterfront drinks in Sausalito, then ferry back past Alcatraz at golden hour.
Cypress cliffs, shipwreck views and haunting bathhouse ruins on the city's wildest edge — the walk-and-talk first date that never misses.
Grand 1898 food hall where the Saturday Foodwise farmers market (8a–2p) is a grazing crawl of oysters, porchetta sandwiches and bay views.
Bernard Maybeck's swan-lagoon rotunda is the most romantic 30 minutes in the city — golden hour here is an unfair advantage.
The evening boat gets you a smaller crowd, cellhouse audio in the dark and the skyline lit up on the ride back — book weeks ahead.
Hang off the running board over Russian Hill, hop out at the crooked block — touristy, sure, and still one of the great cheap thrills in America.
The city's sunniest people-watching lawn — grab Bi-Rite ice cream, claim a slope, and watch all of San Francisco show up on a warm Saturday.
Strong American and global collections, and the free 9th-floor observation tower is a secret 360° view most tourists never find.
Drive up, layer up, and watch the fog river pour over the city at dusk — the classic end to a first date that went well.
Mile of sand with the bridge filling the whole northern sky — bring a jacket and stay for the light show at sunset.
Ferry out, loop the 5-mile Perimeter Road past immigration-station history, and picnic with 360° bay views — a full-day date in one ticket.
Pier 15's giant playground of perception experiments — go Thursday for After Dark (18+, cocktails) when it turns into the smartest bar in town.
Climb the garden stairways past hidden cottages and wild parrots, then take in the 1934 murals and the best close-up skyline panorama.
New parkland stitched over the highway tunnels — campfire circles, food trucks at the Transit Café, and dead-on Golden Gate views.
Rent a pedal boat, circle Strawberry Hill's waterfall island, split snacks at the boathouse — an easy, talky Golden Gate Park classic.
The oldest public Japanese garden in the U.S. — arched drum bridge, koi, and tea service that makes an unhurried conversation easy.
Seven floors of modern heavyweights plus the living wall — a rainy-day date you can stretch into hours without running out of things to say.
Free-entry warehouse of coin-op machines from the 1900s — bring quarters, challenge your date to century-old arm wrestling.
Garlic fries, kayaks waiting for splash hits in McCovey Cove, and the prettiest ballpark backdrop in baseball — great low-pressure hang.
An acoustic sculpture on a Marina jetty that plays the tide through concrete pipes — weird, free, and a guaranteed conversation piece.

nightlife.s: Fillmore boutique club where the room runs hip-hop, R&B and Afrobeats with real headliners passing through — dress up, book a table if flush.
Multi-room SoMa megaclub with an LED cathedral of a main floor — hip-hop nights downstairs in LVL 55 while EDM shakes the ceiling.
The 2024-born warehouse club that revived 11th Street — serious sound, dusk-to-dawn house and techno bookings, Friday and Saturday only.
Art-deco warehouse with a Funktion-One rig — disco, house and the occasional hip-hop takeover for people who actually dance.
Mission backyard institution — cheap drinks, oyster happy hours, and the legendary seasonal Salsa Sunday parties on the patio.
Big Mission salsa palace with live orchestras Friday and Saturday — full dance floor, dressed-up crowd, lessons early if you need them.
The country's first purpose-built jazz hall — world-class bookings in a room with no bad seat; a can't-miss impress-your-date ticket.
Dim Civic Center cocktail den with live jazz seven nights and no cover most of them — first-date insurance in bar form.
Password-at-the-door 1920s speakeasy with library rooms and serious whiskey — book the hidden Wilson & Wilson bar-within-the-bar.
The 1912 hall where Bill Graham built rock history — chandeliers, free apples at the door, and posters for the shows you'll brag about.
John Lee Hooker's old juke joint across from the Fillmore — sweaty funk, soul and boogaloo bands until 2a most weekends.
Downtown K-town-style private suites plus an open-mic main bar — the low-stakes group night that always ends louder than it started.
39th-floor Marriott lounge with fan-window views of the whole glittering city — arrive before sunset, order something brown and slow.
Three-deck rum shrine with 550+ bottles and waterfall decor — the menu is a world tour and the room does half the conversation.
All-night SoMa institution — Bootie mashup Saturdays, goth and hip-hop one-offs, and a 4a license when everything else closes.
Proper Hotel rooftop with fire pits above Market Street — blankets, hot cocktails, and skyline intimacy that photographs like a movie set.

eats.s: Kyoto-kaiseki-inflected omakase in FiDi from a Michelin-recognized counter — the polished special-occasion splurge that earns it.
Twelve seats, four guests per chef, Michelin star — the intimate NoPa counter where every piece comes with a story.
Edomae counter in SoMa that's held a Michelin star since 2016 — Toyosu fish, hushed room, bring someone worth impressing.
The decades-old wharf-adjacent favorite reborn at 430 Folsom with a dry-aging program and Michelin star — SF sushi's glow-up story.
Hayes Valley's hip-hop-soundtracked omakase — inventive nigiri, no dress code, and a price you pick; the fun end of the ladder.
Inner Sunset institution since 1981 — generous nigiri and a chatty counter, the every-month sushi habit rather than the splurge.
Tiny Noe Valley counter punching way above its size — pristine fish and clever sauced pieces without omakase pricing.
Japantown's line-out-the-door hakata tonkotsu — creamy 20-hour broth and firm thin noodles worth every minute of the wait.
Tokyo ramen master Tomoharu Shono's Tenderloin outpost — the toripaitan and A5 wagyu bowls that started SF's ramen arms race.
Chez Panisse-trained izakaya cooking over binchotan — handmade udon, perfect yakitori, and the prettiest courtyard room in the Mission.
Michelin-starred Thai in Japantown — Pim Techamuanvivit's curries and charred prawns make it the city's smartest group dinner.
The Clement Street original whose tea leaf salad, tossed tableside, has kept a line on the sidewalk for two decades.
Corey Lee's charcoal Korean BBQ — Michelin-starred galbi and banchan precision; book ahead, bring carnivores.
Japantown's cheese-capped braised short-rib phenomenon — messy, rich, and built for sharing across the table.

chinese.s: Chinatown's Sichuan standard-bearer — chili-oil wontons and mala chicken from a chef who cooked for presidents; order the explosive pepper dishes.

chinese.n: Chong Qing Xiao Mian 重庆小面
chinese.s: Z&Y alumni slinging Chongqing-style hand-pulled noodles in numbing red broth — the honest 火辣 lunch counter of Kearny Street.
Michelin-starred Cantonese in a grand old Chinatown banquet hall — Dutch crunch BBQ pork and Peking duck for two under lotus chandeliers.

chinese.n: Good Mong Kok Bakery 好旺角
chinese.s: Cash-friendly Stockton Street window where locals queue for har gow, siu mai and BBQ pork buns by the bagful — eat them in Portsmouth Square.
Richmond District's glam Cantonese — five-color soup dumplings and carts by day, all-you-can-eat hot pot by night.
Geary Boulevard dim sum destination the Chronicle keeps on its Top 100 — get the baked BBQ pork buns before 1p or they're gone.
Inner Sunset's cult Shandong house — the dry-fried chicken wings are a city-wide obsession; write your name on the whiteboard and wait.

chinese.n: Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory 金門餅食
chinese.s: Ross Alley's 1962 factory where cookies are still folded by hand off hot irons — 50 cents buys a warm flat one and a great story.

chinese.n: Chinese Historical Society of America 美国华人历史学会
chinese.s: The nation's oldest Chinese-American museum, reopened 2026 in Julia Morgan's landmark YWCA — the context that makes Chinatown click.

chinese.n: Chinese New Year Festival & Parade 舊金山新年大巡遊
chinese.s: America's biggest Lunar New Year parade — 288-foot golden dragon, firecrackers and a million spectators every late Feb–early Mar; 2026's Year of the Horse edition ran March 7.
Grant Avenue's since-1972 wok emporium — Tane Chan's staff will talk you into the right carbon-steel pan and season it with advice.
The Richmond's real eating street — dumplings, roast duck, HK bakeries and Green Apple Books in ten blocks; start at 6th Ave and graze.
Outer Sunset Xi'an specialist — biang biang noodles and cumin lamb burgers that taste like a Silk Road detour off the N-Judah.

chinese.n: Hang Ah Tea Room 杭雅茶室
chinese.s: Tucked in a Chinatown alley since 1920 — America's oldest dim sum house still steaming baskets in a room the size of a train car.
The polished cart-service classic by Rincon Center — Shanghai dumplings and crisp-skin peking duck; pricier, worth it for the ritual.
Since-1972 Hong Kong-style counter on Kearny — shrimp wonton noodle soup in under ten minutes for under fifteen bucks.

chinese.n: New May Wah Supermarket 新美華
chinese.s: Clement Street's workhorse Asian supermarket — Sichuan peppercorns, live fish tanks and every sauce your 川菜 project needs.
Grant Avenue tasting bar where the pourers keep your gaiwan full and the banter flowing — a sneaky-great low-key date stop.

chinese.n: Tin How Temple 天后古廟
chinese.s: The oldest Taoist temple in America (1852), three flights above Waverly Place — incense spirals, harbor goddess, donation entry, quiet awe.

fishing.s: Four generations of Rescinos run this classic wooden boat off Berth 3 — salmon's back for 2026 after the three-year closure, plus halibut, rockfish and crab combos.
Fisherman's Wharf six-pack-to-full-boat operation chasing bay halibut, stripers and ocean rockfish — CA license required aboard, easy walk-on trips.
The Bay Area's storied license-free salmon pier — when the fish run, the rail is elbow-to-elbow; Dungeness crab snares Nov–Jul the rest of the year.
Throw swimbaits into the trough at first light for striped bass all summer — bring a CA license (shore fishing isn't exempt) and respect the rip.
License-free pier at the foot of the Golden Gate — crab pots, jacksmelt and the occasional halibut with the bridge filling your backdrop.
Berkeley Marina's hard-fishing fleet leader — potluck bay trips stacking halibut, stripers and rockfish; license required, gear rentable.
East Bay landing with daily rockfish/lingcod runs to the Farallones and 2026 salmon dates when CDFW windows open — check the season calendar.
SF's own trout-stocked lake — pedal-boat calm, bass in the tules, and a CA license on your phone is all the paperwork.
Horseshoe Cove's license-free pier under the bridge's north tower — jacksmelt, perch and crab with Marin Headlands quiet.
State rec area piers on the bay's warm southeast shore — a striper and sturgeon spot in season, license-free from the piers.

biking.s: Fairfax's famous 9-mile purpose-built loop in the county where mountain biking was born — buy the $5 day pass (Boy Scout land) and earn every bench-cut turn.
The Bay Area's first purpose-built flow trail — 1.5 miles of berms and rollers off the Tamarancho loop; same day pass covers it.
Rare legal state-park singletrack — 12+ swoopy miles of oak-shaded Shoreline and Bay View trails above San Pablo Bay; beginner-friendly, never boring.
Climb the 1896 'Crookedest Railroad' bed from Mill Valley to East Peak — a steady 8-mile grade through the very hills where klunkers invented the sport.
A eucalyptus cloud forest hiding real singletrack in the dead center of the city — fog-slick roots, zero drive time.
SF's biggest dirt network — 7 miles of rideable trail plus the Philosopher's Way loop; scrappy, hilly, and empty on weekdays.
Honest label: mellow bridle paths and Polo Field laps, not singletrack — but it's the easiest spin-and-coffee ride in the city.
The paved standout: a 1.7-mile Headlands climb to the postcard bridge-over-fog shot — pairs perfectly with the Sausalito loop.

biking.n: El Corte de Madera Creek Preserve
biking.s: Midpen's 2,908-acre redwood preserve off Skyline with 34-plus miles of trail — Sierra Morena and the Oljon ridgeline are local favorites. Park at Skeggs Point (approach from the north), helmets required, 15 mph limit.

Over 45 miles of trail across 5,000 acres of oak woodland and volcanic hills east of Santa Rosa, bikes on the designated multi-use trails and fire roads — rocky old basalt-quarry country around Lake Ilsanjo. Day-use fee at the Channel Drive entrance; no e-bikes.

social.s: The world's longest-running free outdoor swing dance (since 1996) on JFK Drive — free beginner lesson at noon, strangers become partners by 12:15.
Mission midweek staple — bachata then salsa-on-2 lessons from 7:30, social dancing to 1:30a; rotation-friendly and beginner-kind.
Live salsa orchestras in a Jackson Square courtyard — dressed-up, dance-first crowd; take the early lesson and stay till close.
The famous MOM weekly — DJ Gordo Cabeza spinning Motown originals and remixes to a packed, friendly floor; $5 after 9p kills your Monday blues.
Thursdays the Academy goes 21+ — DJs under the whale, cocktails by the swamp, planetarium date add-on; the easiest mingling in town.
Free 6:27a Wednesday workout crew — hills, stairs and hugs from strangers who become your people; just show up once.
10k bootcamp run with a boombox — music, exercise stops and a pub finish; pace groups mean nobody gets dropped.
SF's biggest trivia operation runs weeknight quizzes at bars citywide (Spark Social, Patriot House and more) — teams of strangers welcome.

social.n: Chinatown Night Market 唐人街夜市
social.s: Voted the country's #1 night market — five blocks of Grant Avenue food stalls, lion dancers and games on Waverly, second Fridays in season.

social.n: SF Chinese–English Language Exchange 中英语言交流
social.s: Weekly Saturday Mandarin/English tables — half the room wants your English, you want their 中文; RSVP on Meetup for the week's venue.
Roller disco in a deconsecrated 1880s church — disco lights, rental skates, and a floor where laughing at yourself is the icebreaker.
Inner Sunset board game café with hundreds of titles and waffle sandwiches — $7 buys unlimited table time and easy conversation.
Sundays from 7:30a with East Bay Pickup Soccer at Beach Play Field, Piedmont · no Meetup fee.

Join us for our weekly Sunday runs at 10am! Our usual routine is meeting at the southeast corner of the Panhandle (near the William McKinley statue) for a 5K run through Golden Gate Park! Sundays from 10a with Slow Runners Club at Panhandle, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

We play as long as there are 6+ players unless the group decides otherwise. This game is recommended for Intermediate to advanced players. Thursdays from 4p with East Bay Pickup Soccer at Lincoln Square Recreation Center, Oakland · no Meetup fee.
Let’s play some exciting yet competitive tennis. Saturdays from 8:30a with Rossi Racquet Club at Rossi Playground, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Learn How to Dragon Boat with KP Dragons
social.s: Sundays from 8:30a with KP Dragons Dragon Boat Team at Jack London Aquatic Center, Oakland · no Meetup fee.

We keep a moderate pace so no one runs alone – it's a fun run, not all-out. Join for a drink/snack/chat after the run -- we love to meet our neighbors! Mondays from 6:30p with SF Mission Fun Runs at TBD · no Meetup fee.
Let’s play some exciting yet competitive tennis. Sundays from 8:30a with Rossi Racquet Club at Rossi Playground, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Saturday Morning Co-Ed Soccer in the Park
social.s: Friendly full field or half field scrimmages with medium to full sized goals at the Polo Grounds in Golden Gate Park. No slide tackling or rough play. We play just for fun. Saturdays from 8:45a with San Francisco Outdoor Co-Ed Pick-Up Soccer Meetup Group at Golden Gate Park Polo Field, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.
Come join us for San Francisco's Spikeball’s weekly Thursday night pickup. Thursdays from 7:30p with Bay Area Spikeball at Raymond Kimbell Playground Park, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

Whether you’re starting out or looking for a place to play, you’ve landed in the right place. Saturdays from 9a with Ocean Beach Volleyball Training and Playing. San Francisco at Ocean Beach, Stairwell 17, just across from Beach Chalet, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

Every Tuesday Night! Every Tuesday night, come for the tiles and stay for the vibes. This one’s for the Mahjong players. Tuesdays from 7p with Mahjong Night at PanameSF, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

We'll have 2 distance/pace group options for this run. Beginners will do a loop of 3-4 miles at a slower pace, and Intermediate runners can choose the 5-6 mile loop at a faster pace. Thursdays from 6p with Marin Running Club at Tennessee Valley Trailhead/Miwok Stables Parking Lot, Mill Valley · no Meetup fee.

Bachata Lab is San Francisco's Friday night home for Bachata: a weekly class and practice social at the Smuin Center for Dance in Potrero Hill. Fridays from 8p with San Francisco Bachata Classes and Social Dancing at Smuin Ballets SF, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

We compete at local national and international races, and we hold weekly practices that are open to all. Saturdays from 9:30a with Summon The Dragon (Dragon Boat Team) at Grand Street Launching Facility, Alameda · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Oakland Renegades Dragon Boat Team Meetup, Jack London Aquatic Center
social.s: Come join the Oakland Renegades Dragon Boat Team and try out the sport of dragon boating! Saturdays from 10a with Oakland Renegades Dragon Boat Team at Jack London Aquatic Center, Oakland · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Glen Park Canyon hike / Italian, French, German / TextQuilting
social.s: Mondays from 9a with TextQuilting i libri in Italiano, Francese e Tedesco! at Glen Park Canyon, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Backer Beach strolling / TextQuilting / Learn Italian, French, German, Mandarin
social.s: Thursdays from 11:30a with TextQuilting i libri in Italiano, Francese e Tedesco! at Baker Beach, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: SalsaCrazy Mondays in SF - Salsa Lessons and Salsa y Bachata Dance Party
social.s: Join us for SalsaCrazy Mondays - where you can learn to Salsa dance AND show off your skills on the dance floor! No partner or experience required - Learn to Salsa Dance, and dance all night. Mondays from 6:30p with SalsaCrazy's San Francisco Bay Area Salsa Dance Meetup at SalsaCrazy Mondays at Neck of the Woods, san francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Dance Fridays - FUN Salsa Dancing, Bachata Room, Beginning Dance Lessons for ALL
social.s: Fridays from 7p with SalsaCrazy's San Francisco Bay Area Salsa Dance Meetup at Salsa and Bachata at Dance Fridays - Space 550, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Game Night Wednesdays + Happy Hour at Rick & Roxy’s!
social.s: Whether you're rolling in with a crew or flying solo, Game Night Wednesdays is your spot to play, sip, and socialize! Wednesdays from 6p with San Francisco Games at Rick & Roxy's, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Saturday Flow: Qigong for Everyone 大雁功健身
social.s: Join our free weekly sessions to support focus, ease stress, and boost your energy. Limited free parking is available at Marina Green Park, about a 12-minute walk away. Saturdays from 8:30a with Bay Area Wild Goose Qigong 大雁功健身 at Outdoor Patio of Marina Branch Library, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Sundays Pick-Up Soccer in Marina Green
social.s: Lace up your cleats and join us for a pickup soccer game every Sunday at Marina Green. Skill levels vary, but everyone's respectful and just there to have fun. Sundays from 11a with Sundays Pick-Up Soccer in Marina Green at Marina Green, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: When was the last time you played catch?
social.s: No teams. Play Catch. Mondays from 3p with Catch Up at Philz Coffee Truck, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Sensual Bachata Bootcamp (Beginner & Intermediate) Bachata class in SF
social.s: Saturdays from 3p with Bachata and Salsa events in Bay Area at Sensual Bachata & Salsa Academy by Latin Jam, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.
Come join us to practice your Japanese or English! Wednesdays from 5:30p with SF Japanese Language Exchange at Bimi Poke, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

remote.s: Downtown WeWork at California & Kearny, on the Chinatown/FiDi line a short walk up from Union Square — and one of the cheapest WeWork day passes in the city (Salesforce Tower runs $59). Wi-Fi, phone booths, printers, bookable meeting rooms and staffed reception; a coworking membership also opens the other Bay Area WeWorks, including 650 California next door.
remote.b: Open floor has foot traffic and background noise; bring headphones

remote.s: On the 5th & 6th floors of the Grant & Geary Center Building, 77 Geary St, steps off Union Square. Fast Wi-Fi, shared lounges, privacy booths, kitchen with snacks, printer and whiteboards; private offices and team suites upstairs. Day passes are one person, M–F 9a–5p — book through the Industrious app.

Bay Area independent at 235 Pine St in the Financial District, with showers and bike racks. High-speed Wi-Fi, free espresso and coffee, private phone booths, business printers, video-conference rooms, front-desk concierge and mail handling; pet-friendly. Sister spaces at 465 California and 1301 Sansome (rooftop terrace) on the same day pass.
remote.p: Lounge day pass $45 · office day pass $100 · $380/mo lounge · $490/mo dedicated desk

remote.s: Downtown Oakland's homegrown coworking at 1721 Broadway (second site at 2323 Broadway), a block from 19th St BART. Free coffee & tea, meeting rooms, art galleries and a rooftop deck with downtown views; members can add 24/7 access. Open M–F 8a–5p, weekends by appointment.
remote.p: $15 day pass · open coworking from $50/mo · dedicated desk from $250/mo
remote.b: Event-heavy; meeting rooms with partial walls pick up noise from events next door

remote.s: 100 Larkin St at Civic Center, BART/Muni at the door. Free Wi-Fi, public computers and printing, plus 10–12 three-person study rooms — first-come, sign in at the desk, not meant for multi-hour use. Mon 9–6, Tue–Thu 9–8, Fri 12–6, Sat 10–6, Sun 12–6.
remote.b: Quieter on weekdays and early mornings; bright desks face the plaza

remote.s: Members-only library from 1854 at 57 Post St, a block from Union Square — the city's quiet room. Members work on site with Wi-Fi, computers and copiers, take calls in the members' lounge, and get the famous chess room, JSTOR and classes. Library Mon/Wed/Fri 10–6, Tue/Thu 10–8, Sat 10–5; closed Sun. 3rd floor closed for renovation until mid-December.
remote.b: Almost empty on weekday afternoons; reliably quiet for study

remote.s: 125 14th St between downtown Oakland and Lake Merritt, home of the Oakland History Center. Public computers, printing, copier, scanner and fax. Mon–Thu 10–8, Fri 12–5:30, Sat–Sun 10–5:30. Street parking is tight — take BART to 12th St.

SFPUC's 45,000 sq ft community center at 1550 Evans Ave in Bayview, with free Wi-Fi and drop-in public workspaces, and Hungry Cafe downstairs (plenty of outlets, two floors). Public hours M–F 7a–7p; free parking.
Yemeni coffeehouse at 370 4th St in SoMa, ten minutes' walk from Union Square, with Wi-Fi and hours that run until 11p — the late-night laptop option when everything else has closed.
remote.b: Lines and limited seats at peak hours; go off-peak to work

remote.s: 1195 Oak St on the Panhandle: Wi-Fi, abundant outlets, a printer and a quiet second-floor mezzanine. It fills with laptops by day, but there's room.
remote.b: Fills up fast, so arrive early; upstairs nook is quieter

remote.s: Yemeni coffeehouse at 248 9th St in SoMa, a short ride from Union Square. Wi-Fi, and more seats to choose from than most: window-side stools, curved cushioned booths and a big L-shaped couch around an indoor fountain, plus the usual tables. The Infatuation tags it for work and for late nights. Order a Yemeni coffee and a slice of milk cake.
remote.b: Lively and social late at night with group meetups; calmer by day

events.n: Great Dickens Christmas Fair
events.s: Victorian London fills the Cow Palace: costumed characters, music halls, pubs, dance parties and holiday shopping. It's open weekends from 11/21 to 12/20 plus Friday 11/27, 10a–6p. Tickets are online only, and parking is $20.

events.n: Safeway Holiday Ice Rink at Union Square
events.s: Outdoor skating in the middle of Union Square, open daily through mid-January. Check the site for theme nights such as the silent-disco skate.

events.n: 49ers vs. Seahawks
events.s: NFC West rivalry game at Levi's Stadium on Thanksgiving weekend.

events.n: SF Ballet: Nutcracker
events.s: SF Ballet's Nutcracker at the War Memorial Opera House: 35 performances, about two hours each. A 21+ Nutcracker Nightcap party follows opening night (12/4 · 9p), and a sensory-friendly matinee is on 12/27.

events.n: 49ers vs. Rams
events.s: The second Niners–Rams matchup of the season, at Levi's Stadium.

events.n: Victoria Monét: Frequency of Love Tour
events.s: The Grammy-winning R&B singer closes her North American tour at Bill Graham Civic Auditorium. Doors at 7p.

events.n: Ali Wong at the Masonic
events.s: The Bay Area–raised comedian plays three nights of stand-up atop Nob Hill at the Masonic.

events.n: Warriors vs. Nuggets (Christmas Day)
events.s: Steph Curry vs. Nikola Jokić at Chase Center. It's the Warriors' 14th straight Christmas Day game, and the nightcap of the NBA's holiday slate.

events.n: ILLENIUM New Year's Eve
events.s: The melodic bass DJ's three-night New Year's run at Bill Graham Civic Auditorium. The NYE night is sold out, but tickets remain for New Year's Day (1/1).

events.n: Chinese New Year Parade 农历新年大游行
events.s: One of the largest Lunar New Year parades outside Asia, with floats, lion dancers and dragons, welcoming the Year of the Ram (羊). Last year's parade stepped off at dusk from 2nd & Market and wound into Chinatown; get to the curb early. The 2027 start time isn't posted yet.

events.n: Glowfari at Oakland Zoo
events.s: Oakland Zoo's hillside paths glow with giant animal lanterns on most nights. Timed entry runs 4:30–6:30p, and the zoo is closed some Mondays and Tuesdays, on 11/26 and on 12/24–25.

events.n: Christmas in the Park San José
events.s: Free decorated trees, light displays and rides fill Plaza de San José downtown from noon to 10p every day, Christmas included. Opening night on 11/27 at 6p starts with the community tree lighting.

events.n: Deltron 3030 New Year's Eve
events.s: Del the Funky Homosapien, Dan the Automator and Kid Koala play their 2000 sci-fi hip-hop album in full at the Warfield, with Souls of Mischief and DJ Prince Paul. All ages, doors at 8p.

events.n: Cookies Christmas 2026: Berner, Paul Wall & Baby Bash
events.s: SF's own Berner hosts a holiday hip-hop bill at the Warfield with Houston's Paul Wall and Baby Bash. Doors at 7p.

events.n: Trippie Redd: The NDA Tour
events.s: The Ohio rapper and melodic trap star plays the Warfield with TopOppGen, K Suave, BalloutDaDon, Gigi Holland and Goldie. All ages, doors at 7p.

events.n: The Outsiders (Broadway tour)
events.s: The Tony-winning musical adaptation of S.E. Hinton's novel plays a three-week holiday run at the Orpheum Theatre on Market Street.

events.n: Ali Siddiq: The Custom Fit Tour
events.s: The Houston storyteller-comic plays an added early show at the Fox Theater in Oakland (the late show is sold out). Phone-free, ages 16+, doors at 4p.

events.n: Filoli Holiday Lights
events.s: Evening walk through Filoli's decorated historic house and gardens lit with 350,000 lights; timed tickets from $45, last entry 8p.

events.n: Marc Maron: Yammering into the Void Tour
events.s: Marc Maron's early show at the restored Castro Theatre doubles as a live special taping; 18+.

events.n: Winter Walk & Patchwork Show holiday market
events.s: Maiden Lane off Union Square turns into a European-style holiday market of rotating local makers, food and drinks; closed Christmas Day.

events.n: Elf The Musical
events.s: Holiday musical based on the film, following Buddy the elf to New York; a one-week run at the Golden Gate Theatre, about 2.5 hours.

events.n: Stanford vs. San José State (men's basketball)
events.s: Bay Area nonconference matchup at Maples Pavilion as the Cardinal close out December at home before ACC play.

events.n: West Coast Craft Fort Mason Night Market
events.s: Open-air night market of about 60 artists and designers with 25+ Off the Grid food vendors and a full bar on the Fort Mason waterfront.

events.n: Sharks vs. Golden Knights
events.s: Post-Christmas Saturday night hockey at SAP Center as the Sharks host Pacific Division rival Vegas.

events.n: Pura Salsa - Salsa Class - Salsa Social Dance Party - Dj and live percussion
events.s: Saturday from 8p with Bachata & Salsa events in Sf at Muddy Waters, San Francisco · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Barefoot Lake Merritt loop - 1st Sundays at 8:30 am
events.s: We meet weekly Rain or Shine! 3.1 miles around Lake Merritt. If you can run 3 miles in shoes then you can probably do this barefoot. We gather at 8:30 AM and start our run around 8:40 AM. Sunday from 8:30a with Oakland Barefoot Runners Meetup at Lake Merritt Pergola, Oakland · no Meetup fee.

iceskating.s: The downtown holiday rink at 333 Post St, open daily Nov 4, 2026 through Jan 18, 2027. Sessions last an hour and start every 90 minutes; $22 for adults and $17 for kids 8 and under, skates included. Buy tickets ahead online; sessions lost to rain can be rebooked any time before the season ends.

San Francisco's only year-round rink, at 750 Folsom in Yerba Buena Gardens and the city's sole sheet since 1998. The nonprofit Gardens Conservancy took over operations in mid-2026 and upgraded the building. Public sessions run alongside skating school and youth and adult hockey; book on rec.us, where the arena posts its calendar.

The Sharks-run rink at 18th St in Uptown Oakland, a short walk from 19th St BART. Every public session requires online pre-registration, ideally by the day before. Admission is $18, or $27 with rental skates, and Oakland residents with an account get 10% off. Holiday sessions run skate-one, second-same-day-session-half-off.

A recreational-size open-air rink off Middlefield Rd with one of the longest outdoor seasons around: Oct 16, 2026 to Apr 11, 2027, closed Nov 26, Dec 24–25, Jan 1 and Mar 28. Public-session tickets are sold online only, up to 30 days ahead. Gloves are required for every skater, and helmets are recommended for beginners.

A new 6,500 sq ft outdoor rink on the Wharf, open seven days a week from Nov 4, 2026 to Jan 18, 2027 in its first season. Sessions are 75 minutes and tickets run about $20–25 with skate rental included; skaters must be at least 4. It's the waterfront counterpart to the Union Square rink downtown.

Civic Park's holiday rink in downtown Walnut Creek, back for a 21st season Nov 20, 2026–Jan 18, 2027, beside the Frosty's Summit ice slide. Skating is $20 for a 90-minute session, cashless. Non-holiday weekdays open at 4p (to 7:30p Mon–Thu, 10:30p Fri); Sat 11a–10:30p and Sun 11a–8:30p. Holiday periods open at 10a.

City Center Bishop Ranch's rink in San Ramon, open Nov 6, 2026–Jan 3, 2027 and under a canopy for the first time, so it skates rain or shine. Sessions are 90 minutes at 1, 3, 5 and 7p, plus 11a Fri–Sun and 9p Fri–Sat. It's $23, or $16 all day Mon–Tue and at 1 and 3p Wed–Thu, rentals included. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.

Sharks Ice's rink off Old Warm Springs Blvd in south Fremont, the far edge of this list. Public sessions are $18 ($13 for 55+), and rentals are $9 in figure or hockey styles. A 12-admission pack costs $180. The session schedule changes often, so check the day's times and register online before driving down.

skating.s: The skaters' corner of Golden Gate Park, on the old 6th Ave entrance off the car-free JFK Promenade since 1986, repaved with a ground mural in 2022. Weekend rentals, inline or quad, launched in 2024 (Sat–Sun 11a–6p; launch price $20 the first hour for adults, then $5/hr, pads $5/day), bookable on Eventbrite.

skating.n: Golden Gate Park Sunday Roller Disco
skating.s: SF's free weekly dance-skate party at Skatin' Place (6th Ave & JFK), every Sunday since the spot opened in 1986. The 'Godfather of Skate' runs a mobile DJ rig from about noon or 1p to 5p, and on most Sundays someone teaches choreographed roller-disco moves. Bring your own skates or rent on the promenade.

JFK Drive through the middle of Golden Gate Park has been car-free 24/7 since voters passed Prop J in Nov 2022, a fight roller skaters started in the 1970s. It's a wide road surface shared with walkers, bikes and scooters, with about 7 million visits since 2020. Weekends are busiest; Skatin' Place sits on it at 6th Ave.

About 2 miles of the former Upper Great Highway, Lincoln Way to Sloat Blvd, car-free since March 2025 and open 5a–midnight. Voters rejected Prop G on Nov 3, 2026 by 65–35, so it stays a park. Ocean-side road asphalt, with a granite skate area by the Sloat pump track. The road once closed ~27 times a year for sand, so expect drifts after wind.

A 4.5-mile asphalt loop around the lake in the city's southwest corner, and TrailLink lists it for inline skating. It's mostly flat, with parking and restrooms off John Muir Dr at the south end and by the boathouse on the north. Rec and Park has been rebuilding stretches as a new accessible path, so watch for detours.

Marin County Parks' flat, wide 3.7-mile pathway along the edge of Richardson Bay through Bothin Marsh, an asphalt piece of the Bay Trail popular with cyclists, runners and rollerbladers. King tides increasingly flood the marsh section, which the county plans to realign, so check the tide table before a winter skate.

San Francisco's Roller Disco at 554 Fillmore (at Fell), open Tue, Fri, Sat and Sun; closed Mon, Wed and Thu. All-ages sessions are Fri 5–6:30p and Sat 2:30–4p and 4:30–6p, with 18+ nights Fri and Sat 7–11p. Tuesday nights rotate themes: goth, silent disco, guest DJ, K-pop. Tickets are sold per session online.

A 3.1-mile path around the lake in downtown Oakland, from Lake Merritt Blvd to Lakeside Park, which TrailLink lists for inline skating, biking and walking. The surface is concrete rather than asphalt, so expect more buzz and seams than on a fresh blacktop path; softer wheels help.

skating.n: Iron Horse Trail (San Ramon–Dublin skate stretch)
skating.s: The 32-mile asphalt rail-trail along I-680, Concord to Livermore. A TrailLink inline reviewer skates Dougherty Rd to Bollinger Canyon Rd regularly and calls the pavement fairly good with few cracks; north of Bollinger it turns to concrete with expansion joints. Weekends bring bikes, joggers and kids, and street crossings are frequent.

A paved multi-use path behind Alameda's 2.5-mile bay beach, running from Crab Cove east toward the Elsie Roemer marsh with the dunes on one side and Shoreline Dr on the other. A state-beach guide calls it flat and smooth enough for inline skates. The paved path ends past Broadway. Park lots are $5 and cashless; gates close at 7p.

coffee.s: Nob Hill café at 1191 Pine St, in Polk Gulch, about a 15-minute walk uphill from Union Square. Fast Wi-Fi, laptops allowed and both seats and outlets rated abundant, a rare combination this close to downtown. Coffee, tea and light café food.

The SF-born chain's Civic Center shop at 399 Golden Gate Ave, by the federal buildings and UC Law SF. Wi-Fi, laptops allowed, plenty of seats and a reasonable number of outlets; the best chain bet for a laptop near City Hall. Philz's made-to-order pour-overs, Mint Mojito included.

SoMa roaster at 1415 Folsom St, known for Ethiopian single-origin beans roasted in-house. Wi-Fi and laptops allowed, with a modest number of seats; good for a focused morning rather than a full day. Espresso, pour-overs and pastries.

Roomy, sunlit café at 790 Lombard St on the North Beach side of Russian Hill. Fast Wi-Fi, laptops allowed, abundant seating and enough outlets to go around. Coffee, fruit shakes, sandwiches and pastries; handy before or after a climb up to Coit Tower.

Lower Haight institution at 508 Haight St, at Fillmore: a big, worn-in room with couches, lots of tables and a back garden. Fast Wi-Fi, laptops allowed and outlets rated adequate. Casual coffee and food, with the neighborhood's regulars as company.

Mission mainstay at 3049 20th St, at Alabama: a massive indoor room plus a back patio. Fast Wi-Fi, laptops allowed, abundant seating and enough outlets. A sizable sandwich menu, and beer and wine for when the workday ends.

Bernal Heights café at 400 Cortland Ave with many indoor tables and a big outdoor patio the free, fast Wi-Fi reaches. Laptops allowed, with seats and outlets both rated abundant. Wraps, sandwiches and salads, plus beer and wine.

Cole Valley roaster at 672 Stanyan St, across from Golden Gate Park: high ceilings, a large floor and a back patio. Wi-Fi that reviewers call fast and laptops allowed; outlets aren't listed, so arrive charged. House-roasted espresso drinks.

Dogpatch café at 2535 3rd St with two levels of seating and Wi-Fi, on The Infatuation's 2026 list of SF coffee shops for getting work done. Espresso, matcha and a steamed-egg breakfast sandwich; a good base near the Dogpatch galleries and the Muni T line.

Marina roastery at 2331 Chestnut St with spread-out seats that give you some privacy. Wi-Fi, laptops allowed, and both seating and outlets rated abundant. Coffee roasted on site and a breakfast menu; the Marina Green and the bay are a few blocks north.

Corner café at 1799 McAllister St, at Baker, in the North of Panhandle neighborhood. Fast Wi-Fi, laptops allowed and an adequate number of seats and outlets; a calm neighborhood room near the Panhandle and Alamo Square. Espresso drinks and pastries.

Castro café at 3985 17th St, a couple of blocks from Castro Station. Wi-Fi, laptops allowed, and seats and outlets both rated abundant, so it's one of the easiest full-day laptop spots in the neighborhood. Coffee drinks and café bites.

The Yemeni coffeehouse's SoMa room at 370 4th St, near Moscone Center. Free Wi-Fi, laptops allowed and a fair number of seats and outlets; open until 11p, hours few SF cafés keep. Order a Yemeni latte with bee bites or a slice of milk cake.

pickleball.s: Eight dedicated pickleball courts in the Sunset's Larsen Park (19th Ave and Wawona), opened in December 2023 and among the city's biggest sets. All eight are kept for open play, so there is nothing to reserve: show up and join the rotation. Nets provided; no lights, so it is a daylight game.

Six dedicated courts at Louis Sutter Playground in McLaren Park (University and Wayland, Portola). None are reservable: all six run as first-come open play with nets provided. No lights; the park is open 6a to 10p and has restrooms on site.

Golden Gate Park's tennis center has five lit pickleball courts with nets provided, all reservable. Since July 2026 a court costs $10/hr for residents or $16 for nonresidents on weekdays 7a to 3p, and $12 or $20 in prime time (weekday evenings and weekends); seniors 65+ pay $5 weekday mornings.

Six courts in the Marina, lit for evening play with rolling nets; four can be booked at $5 a court-hour on rec.us/sfrecpark. Courts 3 and 4 hold open group play Mon and Wed 7a to 3p, Sat 7a to 5p, and 7 to 9a on the other mornings before tennis takes over.

Nine courts at Arguello and Anza in the Inner Richmond: five reservable at $5 an hour on rec.us/sfrecpark, four walk-up, with rolling nets plus a permanent one on Court E. Court 3 runs open group play Tue, Thu and Fri 9a to 3p and Sun 9a to 5p. No lights.

Six courts at Stern Grove in the Parkside, four of them bookable for $5 a court-hour on rec.us/sfrecpark (slots open at 8a, seven days ahead), with four rolling nets supplied. No lights. A booked court left empty for 15 minutes opens to walk-up play.

pickleball.n: Willie Woo Woo Wong Playground pickleball court
pickleball.s: The Chinatown playground's single lit court is the closest public pickleball to Union Square, a short walk up Sacramento St. It is walk-up only, with no reservations and no fee, but bring your own net. Good for a quick game; for a real rotation head to Larsen or Louis Sutter.

Indoor gym pickleball at 100 Collingwood St in the Castro, on three courts with nets provided. The fall 2026 drop-in schedule runs Thu and Fri noon to 3:30p plus Fri 5 to 8p through December, no reservation needed. The gym timetable changes by season, so check before going.

The Inner Richmond rec center at 251 18th Ave holds indoor pickleball drop-in on four gym courts with nets provided: Thu 10:30a to 1:30p and Sat 9:30a to 1:30p on the fall schedule, through late December. The rainy-day option for players from Rossi and Goldman nearby.

Oakland's indoor pickleball social club in Temescal (4000 Telegraph Ave): four cushioned courts, a cafe and wine bar, sauna and lounge, open 8a to 10p daily. Guests are welcome: open play by level is $15 to $30 a session (2.5 hours, eight per court), courts $60/hr, paddle rental $5.

Padel and pickleball club at 1070 Maryland St in Dogpatch, one of Bay Padel's two SF sites (the other is on Treasure Island). Non-members pay $20 a court-hour at peak (weekdays from 4p, weekends) and $15 off-peak; two-hour round-robin open plays for all levels are $35, booked on the Bay Padel app.
